utterances.text: Yes, I think that if you want to talk about other people who were along with Mr. K, we should have a private session, because you know that some of these people may be called to the Court to testify and they should be protected even at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, I agree, yes. I accept that we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let us move into private session. Madam Registrar, will you call the technical booth.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Par. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Let us go back to that day. Do you remember who is it that brought you from Heliodrom to the place where the incident took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly who was it that drove us there but I know that as I -- when I worked there, I know that there was a gentleman who drove us and who drove a vehicle we called the Deutz. I believe his name was Dinko, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Right. So when you arrived there, you said you sat down and were sitting until allegedly Stela came?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: Yes. We were sitting next to the house where we were to work later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did anyone guard you? Were there any guards around you? How was it organised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: Well, there were soldiers around, there were soldiers there. Whether their role was to guard us or whether their role was simply to watch us, I can't say. I do not really know what their role was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Witness K, you were a prisoner of war. You must know what it means to be watched and what it means to be a captive and to be guarded. So when that group arrived, was this group guarded, which meant whether its movement was controlled, what each one of them was to do, to see that they wouldn't escape. In that sense, were there guards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: Yes, in that case were there guards because we did not move anywhere, we just sat there in one place. We did not walk around. We did not simply move around anywhere. Furthermore, you know it -- well, you were not in my place, but I was. When you are faced with such a situation, then you practically try not to even to bat an eyelid, let alone move around. So I didn't really look around. I didn't try to see what was going on and how it was. I suppose it must have been the fear that I felt.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Witness K, my question having to do with the guard was meant to establish whether it was a particular unit that guarded you, whether that was a unit, a specific unit or some specific soldiers. I simply wanted to verify your story about this incident. So that is why I'm asking you whether there was somebody issuing orders there to help us identify the persons and the unit which was there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: I cannot tell you that, whether it was these men or those others who guarded us. I can tell you it was a soldier or several soldiers who guarded us but I didn't look around so I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So can we then infer that you believe that you were under some kind of military supervision?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: Well, yes. Of course we were under supervision.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And the name of any one of those soldiers who supervised you, can you give me any of the names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: No, I didn't know any one of them. How could I know them?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And then Stela came. How did he come?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: He came from up there, from the entrance to the yard of that house. I told you I didn't know who he was. He came in a vehicle and then he came in on foot. I don't know what kind of vehicle it was, to tell you the truth, and he was followed by this other gentleman that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: You don't know the -- anything about the vehicle but do you know whether it was yellow, blue, a truck, a jeep or anything? You don't have to give me the make, the brand.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Slowly, please, excuse me. I will be asking you the questions because you have already told us the whole story. So he came out of the car. Was he alone or with this same or with someone else or was anyone else with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: I didn't notice. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Can we remember what he looked like, what he had on, as regards Stela and this other person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: I have described his face for you as I remember them. To tell you the honest truth, I am unable to describe to you now what clothing they were wearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: What about weapons? Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: I didn't notice that either, because we were all standing with our heads bowed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: As far as I remember, you said you were sitting down and that was what provoked the whole incident.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: Yes, but when the gentleman approached to about ten metres away from us, the cursing started, the order to stand at attention, so we were standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: When did you learn that this was Stela?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: As he approached, he said that that was his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did anyone of the prisoners say, "Here comes Stela," or something to that effect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Is Stela in the courtroom now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Could you please identify him. Look at him and tell us where he is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: The gentleman over there, with the headphones on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: You see what he looks like now. How did he look then as compared to what he looks like now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: As far as his face is concerned, and his physical appearance, there is virtually no difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: But a long time has gone by; eight years.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't look very closely at the gentleman.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Have you seen him on television recently or in the newspapers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: I'm not really following the media too much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Sema Bosnjic, do you remember any details about him and his appearance, what he looked like, how he was armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: Sema, I just saw him the way he walked. I know that he limped and I remember very well that he had a big scar on his forehead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: When did you learn that that was Sema Bosnjic and who told you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: I learned that also from the soldiers who were saying that that was he. They even said that he was Mr. Stela's deputy. Whether that is true or not, I don't know. That is what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you know whether Sema was a Muslim or a Croat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: Judging by his name, I assume he was a Muslim, but what his options were, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So you assume?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: You do have some information about him, as you have told us, that he may have been killed. Do you know how his scar came into being? So it's not -- it's not possible for you not to know something that is obvious, whether he was a Muslim or not.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: Well, you see, for me, that doesn't matter what ethnicities or religion a person is. For me, what is important is that he's a good human being.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So Stela and Sema arrived, and on that occasion, one of the prisoners was beaten up, and we won't mention his name now. So one prisoner was beaten up, the one we mentioned; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Were you beaten up on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you tell this story in a different way ever? But to be more specific, let me ask you more specifically. On the 6th of July, 1995, did you tell the police in Mostar that you were beaten by Stela?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: I never said that, and if it says anything else in the statement, those are not my words. And if that is what is written in the statement, I had no intention of incriminating anyone or facilitating anyone's position. I'm here to tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: I will show you now the statement, and the part has been highlighted where it says that, so please review that statement. When I say "review it," look at the header, where it says which institution took the statement from you, check your particulars and your signature, please, and then you will answer some questions linked to that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask the usher, please ...

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Par, shouldn't we go into private session? Because the document will certainly contain elements that might identify the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Mr. Fourmy. Thank you very much for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K
utterances.text: As far as I know and as far as I remember, it was known as Kajtaz's house. That is the information I have. I described where it was situated. I said that across the way was another unit with the graffiti on the wall. It said "Benko Penavic."

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I don't have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Prosecutor. Witness K, you have completed your deposition. Thank you for the information you have conveyed. You will be able to leave. Please don't move until the usher has pulled down the blinds. I take advantage of the opportunity to thank you once again for your deposition and to wish you a safe journey to your country of residence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor, for your next witness, how do we stand regarding protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Fourmy. Our next witness is protected by a pseudonym and has facial distortion.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. The witness's pseudonym will be L.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. Can you hear me, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You asked for certain protective measures consisting of facial distortion on the videotape and on the screen, and you will also have a pseudonym, and that is Witness L. So please don't be offended. That is the only way we will be able to address you. You will be, for us, Witness L. Is that agreed? Before you start with your deposition, will you please read the solemn declaration given to you by the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Please take a seat --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and make yourself as comfortable as possible. Please feel at ease. We're just trying to learn from you what you know, and for that purpose will you try and answer as precisely as possible, listening carefully to the questions put to you. Mr. Usher, could you show the witness, please, the document with his name on it. Witness L, don't pronounce your name. Just tell us whether that is your name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. So it will first be the Prosecutor who will have questions for you and then it will be the turn of the Defence. Having said that, I don't think that we will have time for questions from the Defence this evening, so, Mr. Prosecutor, please begin with your examination-in-chief, and thank you in advance.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Fourmy, and may I ask that for the first couple of questions we can go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Madam Registrar. Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Witness L, do you know of a village named Rastani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And do you know what happened to Rastani on the 20th of September 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Could you tell us about this.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: On the 20th of September 1993, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina captured Rastani and placed it under its control.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And were you present on that day in Rastani, as a member of the Bosnian army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: I was not. Only when darkness fell, in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So you went to Rastani in the evening on the 20th of September 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Until the next day, in the evening, that is the 21st, in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Where did you go on the 21st?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: I went to Vrapcici.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And where is Vrapcici located in relation to Rastani? North, south, east or west from Rastani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: East, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: How far is Vrapcici from Rastani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Three, four kilometres, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. Prosecutor. For the transcript perhaps we should have the spelling, because if we need to find these places on the map -- and I do apologise, but these -- this geographical information goes beyond my abilities. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Witness L, can could you spell the name of the village Vrapcici, spell it in your own language, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: V-r-a-p-c-i-c-i, both Cs with diacritical marks.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Thank you. And where did you stay in Vrapcici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: In a house.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, what happened in Rastani in the days after you left Rastani and went to Vrapcici? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: I did not -- I do not know what period of time you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: (redacted) attack on Rastani.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And with whom did you go back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: What's his name?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: His last name?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And did you go back to Rastani to assist your colleagues in defending the village of Rastani? Was that the purpose of your return to Rastani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Yes, we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you encounter somebody when you arrived in Rastani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: We came across a group carrying the wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Were these Muslim soldiers, this group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: They were members of the Armija, yes. And there were civilians Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. amongst them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: How many civilians were amongst this group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Two, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Can you tell me who it was? Can you tell me his name?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you speak with Safet Memic on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: What did Safet Memic tell you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Well, he said they had been brought here by the troops, and that he had fled over to this side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And when he said that he was brought by the troops, which troops was he referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: The HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And where had the soldiers taken him from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: From the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And did he tell you what he -- what he needed to do for the HVO soldiers when he was taken to Rastani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: He didn't describe his job to me in very precise terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: What did he say in general terms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: That he was sent ahead of them so as to reconnoitre the positions and then come back.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And he didn't come back, but on that occasion, he fled? Is that what he said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, what happened after you had encountered this group of Muslim soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, excuse me, Witness. Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Fourmy. I apologise to you, Mr. Bos. I counted questions. I was reluctant to interrupt you but this was the fourth leading question, so let us not waste time discussing this further. I'd merely like to ask you to phrase your questions properly, proper in the proper manner for direct examination. Thank you, and once again, my apologies for interrupting.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: May I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Krsnik. Mr. Prosecutor, I hope you will take note of this objection and please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So what happened after you had encountered this group of Muslim soldiers? What happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: We moved on towards the positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Then what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Meanwhile, there was fierce artillery fire and we took shelter in a house.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of the house, who it belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: The house has no name to it, but that area, that locality is called Dumpor's houses. It is a cluster of houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: What happened after you had taken shelter in the Dumpor houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: We waited for the artillery fire to stop, and after a while, we heard voices outside. So we peeped out, and at that moment, we saw rifles aimed at us and heard a call to come out. And we came out, and we noticed that it -- that they were -- that those soldiers were members of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: How many HVO soldiers did you see at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: About ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And do you know from which units these soldiers were, which HVO units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Not at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: But later on, you did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Later on, I learned that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And what did you learn later on? Which units were they from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: That they were members of an ATG group from Mostar and an ATG group from Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: How come that you learned that they were from an ATG group Listica and an ATG group from Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: I learned that they were from Mostar ATG because there was there Miro Kolobara. He was with that group, and later on, he was in the same prison that I was in, in Ljubuski. And that is where I learned that he was a member of the Mostar ATG.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And how did you learn that there were also soldiers from the ATG Listica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Because we were taken to Listica because that group captured us and they took us to their seat.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Just to clarify, Witness L, Listica, is that another name for Siroki Brijeg? Are Listica and Siroki Brijeg the same name for the same village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Yes. They are two names for one and the same town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, let's go back to this group of ten HVO soldiers, you said. So you've mentioned one person, Mr. Kolobara. Did you recognise any other person in that group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: I did. I recognised a person whose nickname was Splico.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Where did you know him from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: I met him in 1992, in the north camp. That is where an HVO unit was quartered. And on one occasion I was present when he came and I heard other people calling out to him. Otherwise, his appearance is quite characteristic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you know where this a.k.a. Splico, where he came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, this group which arrested you, were they all soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: There were some civilians among them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And what did they do, these civilians in that group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: I spotted that one of them had grenades, grenades for the hand-held mortar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Would you know what kind of ethnicity these two persons were who -- these two civilians were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: What happened after you were arrested at the Dumpor houses? What did the soldiers do to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: We were beaten there. They hit us with rifle butts and their hands, and kicked us. They brought a cannister full of petrol from somewhere and they poured petrol over my colleague. They gave us bank notes to chew them and swallow them. And it went on for about half an hour, maybe an hour, and then they left. Most of them left. Only two stayed behind with us, until darkness fell. And when darkness fell, a shift came and took us towards Bakijina Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: How did you go towards Bakijina Luka? Did you go by car or by foot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: On foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And what happened when you arrived at Bakijina Luka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: When you arrived at Bakijina Luka, where were you taken next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: From Bakijina Luka, we were put in a van and taken to Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: And did people beat you in the van?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So then you arrived in Siroki Brijeg. You were still together with your friend Arif Maric; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Where were you taken in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: They took us to the tobacco station at Siroki Brijeg and they brought us to a building, into a room where there were six or seven men in uniforms, persons in uniforms, who asked questions, pushing us, striking us. Then they took me out of that room and into another room. There were two or three persons in that room; I'm not sure. One of them hit me with his foot in the chest. But I wasn't there long in that room.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: The person who actually hit you in the chest, could you describe that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: That man looked around 50 years of age, with a grey beard, medium height, around 180, 185 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Was he wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: What kind of uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: A camouflage, a military uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you remember whether it had a patch on the uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So what happened after you were kicked and beaten by these two or three persons? What happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Then I was taken out of the building through the entrance, to the front door, and I was there for a while - I don't know - and after that I do not remember anything until the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Just let me go back. So you were taken outside in front of the tobacco building, and you said that you sat there, and then you say you don't remember. Why don't you remember what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: As the soldiers were passing by, they would hit me, and I suppose that after one of such blows, I fainted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, when you recovered, where were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: I was in a room about a metre and a half by three metres, without any furniture. There was nothing in it. One wall was tin plate and there were no windows in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Was anyone in the room adjacent to you, the room which was against the wall which was tin-plated, adjacent to the tin-plated wall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: In that other room -- my colleague was in that other room.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: That was Arif Maric. And --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... communicate with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: How was that possible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Because there was only that tin plate between us. We could not see one another, but we could hear one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, later on that day, did they put a bed in your cell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Later on, yes, a bed was brought in.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Is it correct that after 12 days, Arif Maric was actually also brought in your cell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: That's right. After 12 days, he was transferred from his to my cell, because another prisoner had been brought to his cell.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, and thank you for giving me the floor. My apologies to Mr. Bos. You know that we are listening with great attention to your questions, and the last three questions were again highly leading, but I am objecting only to this last question. I think it should be phrased differently. And please don't Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. misunderstand me. I'm not trying to suggest anything, to insinuate anything, or to interfere with your direct examination in any way, but I only want to ask you to rephrase these questions and the questions that will follow. Thank you very much for your understanding, and once again, my apologies for interrupting.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: May I respond? I realise that the last couple of questions were leading, but I did that on purpose to speed up this examination, and I don't think it's of such importance that these questions need to be put in a different way. But if counsel insists, I will refrain from doing it. It will take a little longer then.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are here to learn, as you know, so I think it is owing to this joint effort that we can arrive at the best procedure. Now, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: When Arif Maric was brought in to your cell, did the guards actually put an extra bed in the cell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction, interpreter's correction, the answer is, "No, we shared one bed."

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Could you tell the Court how many days you were in the cell together with Arif Maric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: I wouldn't know exactly but I'd say about 40 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Could you tell us about the food that you were provided when you were detained in the tobacco station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: We were getting some dry pack. In the beginning, for the first few days, regularly, one meal a day. Then it began to happen every second day. Once we received our next ration after three days. And what we were given was about half a loaf of bread, or one loaf, some margarine and some marmalade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Could you go to the toilet? What happened when you needed to go to the toilet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: We would go to the toilet on those occasions when they brought us food. It was the only time they opened the door and allowed us to go to the WC.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, on the second day that you were detained in the tobacco station, do you remember what happened on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: I remember it, yes. That day, they first took Arif away, and after a while, I heard screams. I recognised his voice. And a little later, he was brought back. And then they took me along, and they took me to the upper floor. And upstairs, there was a member in a uniform, and he took my particulars, that is my name, place of residence and suchlike, and then I was taken back to the cell. They did not beat me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, you said that you heard Arif Maric scream. Did you later find out what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Yes. Later on, he told me that they applied current from the army telephone, that is the wires, and they would place them on the -- on his hands and they would start winding up the inductor telephone so that he would receive those shocks.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Now, at one moment, Arif Maric was put in your cell and you said that other people were put in his cell; is that correct? Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor, excuse me for interrupting but it is two minutes past 5.00. I was wondering whether this would be a fresh area so maybe it would be an appropriate time to break for this evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I think we will stop there for today. I thank both parties for the way we worked today because I think we have made some very good progress. Witness, please don't move, remain seated. The usher will accompany you out after he has pulled down the blinds. We will meet here again tomorrow at quarter past 9.00. So I hope you have a pleasant evening and tomorrow, we will proceed in a satisfactory manner, I hope. Thank you. The hearing is adjourned to tomorrow morning at 9.15.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOURMY
utterances.text: 5.03 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday the 2nd day of August 2001, at 9.15 a.m.
